concept.title: Dates
concept.shortdesc: How uFTi records a date, including one that you only know in part or are not sure of.

conbody.p: Most dates in a family tree are not exact. A record may give only a year. A story may say a birth was "about 1850". uFTi lets you record a date as well as you know it. Then the tree never claims more than your evidence does.

section.title: How much you know
section.p: The date editor asks . Choose , or , to match what the record gives you. Do not make up a day or a month to fill the gap.

section.title: How sure you are
section.p: Choose to show the choices under .

dlentry.dd: A record or a story gives a date that is close, but not exact.
You worked the date out yourself, for example from an age.
It happened on or before this date. A baptism date can be a limit like this for a birth.
It happened on or after this date.
You know the earliest and the latest date it could have been. Enter both.
Something went on for a while, such as a job or a stay. Enter the start and the end.

section.title: Typing the date
section.p: Choose to type the whole date in one box. uFTi shows how the date reads, so that you can check it. If uFTi does not understand what you typed, it tells you.

section.title: Calendars
section.p: Almost every date uses the calendar that you use today. If a record uses an older one, choose it under .
